CausalChain: NAFLD-induced metabolic stress -> Upregulation of FTO (via stress-responsive transcription factors) -> FTO-mediated m6A demethylation on select lipid metabolism gene mRNAs -> Enhanced mRNA stability and translation -> Overproduction of lipid metabolic enzymes -> Accumulation of lipotoxic metabolites -> Amplification via ROS and α-dicarbonyl stress -> Activation of inflammatory pathways (RNF5/IGF2BP1 axis and RAGE signaling) -> Recruitment of immunosuppressive cells (Tregs, MDSCs) -> Formation of a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment -> Progression to hepatocellular carcinoma
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that NAFLD-induced metabolic stress triggers an early, stress-responsive upregulation of FTO in hepatocytes through factors such as PPARγ. FTO then selectively demethylates m6A marks on mRNAs that encode pivotal lipid metabolic enzymes, leading to enhanced stability and translation of these transcripts. The resulting overproduction of lipid metabolizing enzymes causes an accumulation of lipotoxic metabolites, which further increases cellular ROS and α-dicarbonyl stress. This amplified oxidative environment cooperates with FTO-driven metabolic changes to activate alternative inflammatory pathways, specifically the RNF5/IGF2BP1 axis and RAGE signaling. Consequently, these events promote the recruitment of immunosuppressive cells, thereby establishing a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment that drives the progression from NAFLD to hepatocellular carcinoma. This hypothesis will be tested and validated using integrated omics methodologies (single-cell RNA-seq, m6A-RIP-seq, spatial transcriptomics) coupled with functional studies to dissect the molecular and cellular causality underlying this cascade.
Abstract: We propose that in hepatocytes exposed to NAFLD-induced metabolic stress, there is an early stress-responsive induction of FTO that serves as a pivotal integrator linking metabolic imbalance, oxidative stress, and immune modulation. Specifically, FTO is selectively upregulated—potentially via stress-activated transcription factors such as PPARγ—and removes m6A modifications from a subset of mRNAs encoding key lipid metabolic enzymes. This demethylation increases the stability and translation of these transcripts, thereby enhancing enzyme production and driving the accumulation of lipotoxic metabolites. The ensuing buildup of toxic lipid intermediates amplifies reactive oxygen species (ROS) and α-dicarbonyl stress, which in turn synergize with FTO-mediated metabolic dysregulation to activate alternative inflammatory cascades including the RNF5/IGF2BP1 axis and RAGE signaling. These integrated stress responses foster the recruitment of immunosuppressive cells (e.g., regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells), collectively creating a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment that propels the progression from NAFLD to hepatocellular carcinoma. We will leverage state-of-the-art omics technologies such as single-cell RNA-seq, m6A-RIP-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to precisely identify FTO’s mRNA targets, delineate the temporal cascade of these events, and validate the functional interplay between these pathways, thereby providing novel insights and therapeutic targets.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis linked NAFLD metabolic stress to FTO-mediated m6A demethylation of lipid metabolic enzyme mRNAs, culminating in lipotoxic metabolite accumulation and inflammatory signaling leading to HCC. The revised hypothesis retains the same causal chain but refines it by: (1) emphasizing the upstream regulation of FTO (e.g., via PPARγ and other stress-responsive factors), (2) detailing the selectivity of FTO towards critical mRNA targets for lipid metabolism, (3) clarifying the downstream contributions of enhanced ROS and α-dicarbonyl stress in synergizing with inflammatory pathways (specifically the RNF5/IGF2BP1 axis and RAGE signaling), and (4) explicitly incorporating current omics technologies for target identification and mechanistic dissection. This improved version not only reinforces each critical step of the original causal reasoning but also enhances practical implementability and novelty by integrating precise molecular profiling strategies.
